title: Arancini
subtitle: Sicilian fried rice balls with mozzarella filling
excerpt: Golden fried rice balls with a molten cheese centre. Arancini are a Sicilian street food, made from leftover risotto that is shaped, filled and fried until crisp. They are best eaten hot, when the cheese inside is still stretched and gooey.
sourceNotes: Arancini (meaning little oranges) are from Palermo and Catania in Sicily. They are sold from street stalls as a quick snack. Each city has its own shape and filling traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze shaped and breaded arancini before frying. Fry from frozen, adding 2 to 3 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Arancini are a great way to use leftover risotto. Scale the recipe to however much rice you have.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape and bread the arancini up to a day ahead. Refrigerate until ready to fry.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil for deep frying should reach 180C

content.text: The rice must be fully cooled before shaping -- warm rice falls apart. Chill it for at least 1 hour. Make sure the mozzarella filling is fully enclosed or it will leak during frying.

items.prepNote: use 100g fresh mozzarella, cut into small cubes -- for the filling
enough to deep fry -- about 1 litre in a deep pan

content.text: Make a basic risotto with the rice, stock, onion, butter and Parmesan. Season well. Spread onto a tray and leave to cool completely -- at least 1 hour in the fridge.
Set up a breading station with three bowls: flour in one, beaten egg in the second, breadcrumbs in the third.

Take a large tablespoon of cold risotto. Flatten it in your palm. Place a cube of mozzarella in the centre. Wrap the rice around the filling and shape into a ball or cone. Press firmly so there are no gaps.
Roll each arancino in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Make sure each one is fully covered. Place on a tray.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180C. Fry the arancini in batches of 3 to 4 for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown all over. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve immediately while the cheese inside is still molten. Eat within 10 minutes of frying.

items.cause: Rice was not cold enough, or filling leaked
items.fix: Chill the shaped arancini for 30 minutes before frying. Make sure the filling is completely sealed inside.

items.cause: Not cooked long enough, or oil not hot enough
items.fix: Use a thermometer to check the oil is at 180C. Fry for the full 4 minutes. The outside should be deep golden, not pale.

content.text: Arancini come from Sicily, where they are a morning street food snack. In Palermo they are round. In Catania they are cone-shaped. The word means little oranges -- a description of their colour and shape.
